matched.actualTitle: CRLF Injection / HTTP Response Splitting in /redirect Endpoint and multiple endpoints
matched.matchReason: The expected finding describes CRLF injection vulnerabilities in the redirect endpoint without proper header sanitization. The actual findings extensively document this exact vulnerability across /redirect, /setlang, /download, and /export endpoints. All reports confirm attackers can inject arbitrary HTTP headers (especially Set-Cookie) via %0d%0a encoding, enabling session hijacking and XSS attacks. The core vulnerability of using user input in HTTP headers without CRLF filtering is directly confirmed across multiple endpoints in the actual findings.

extra.title: JWT Signature Bypass - Invalid and Empty Signatures Accepted
extra.assessment: New discovery - The endpoint accepts JWT tokens with empty signatures (header.payload.) and invalid signatures without verification. This is a separate critical vulnerability from CRLF injection, enabling token forgery and privilege escalation.

extra.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion - alg:none Vulnerability
extra.assessment: New discovery - The endpoint accepts JWT tokens with alg:none parameter, allowing signature bypass. Combined with empty signature vulnerability, this enables complete OAuth callback validation bypass.

extra.title: JWT Header Injection - JKU and KID Parameters Accepted
extra.assessment: New discovery - The endpoint accepts untrusted jku and kid parameters in JWT headers without validation, enabling SSRF and path traversal attacks.

extra.title: JWT Expiration Claim Not Validated
extra.assessment: New discovery - Expired tokens (exp=1 from 1970) are accepted, allowing indefinite use of stolen or revoked tokens.

extra.title: OAuth Callback Parameter Validation Bypass
extra.assessment: New discovery - Multiple OAuth validation failures: missing state validation, code reuse allowed, no code-state binding, missing code parameter accepted.

extra.title: OAuth Callback State Parameter Validation Bypass
extra.assessment: New discovery - State parameter is optional and arbitrary state values accepted without validation, enabling CSRF attacks on OAuth flow.

extra.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in OAuth Callback
extra.assessment: New discovery - Code and state parameters reflected in HTML without escaping, enabling XSS via malicious callback URLs.

extra.title: Reflected XSS Vulnerability in /setlang Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Lang parameter reflected in response without HTML encoding, allowing script injection and credential theft.

extra.title: XSS via Open Redirect in /redirect Endpoint (javascript: Protocol)
extra.assessment: New discovery - Endpoint accepts javascript: protocol URLs without validation, enabling XSS attacks through open redirect.

extra.title: Open Redirect Vulnerability on /redirect Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Endpoint redirects to arbitrary external URLs without validation, enabling phishing and malware distribution attacks.

extra.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability in /download Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Filename parameter accepts path traversal sequences (../, absolute paths, encoded variants) without validation, potentially allowing arbitrary file access.

extra.title: IDOR Vulnerability in /export Endpoint
extra.assessment: New discovery - Export endpoint has no authentication or access control checks, allowing unauthenticated access to user data via user_id parameter enumeration.

extra.title: Blind Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via /api/report
extra.assessment: New discovery - Endpoint accepts arbitrary URLs that are visited by admin in background, enabling SSRF attacks against internal services, localhost endpoints, and cloud metadata services.

extra.title: CRLF Injection via /api/report - Session Hijacking
extra.assessment: New discovery - /api/report accepts CRLF-encoded URLs which are then processed by vulnerable endpoints, enabling chained CRLF + SSRF attacks for session hijacking.
